en: Chapter on Mindfulness, Section 7: The Question on the Distinction between One Possessed of Lust and One Free from Lust.
“Venerable Nāgasena, what is the difference between one who is possessed of lust and one who is free from lust?
“Great King, one is attached, while the other is unattached.”
“What is this, venerable sir, that is called ‘clinging’ and ‘non-clinging’?
“One person, great king, desires; another does not desire.

“I see such a thing, venerable sir: both one who has lust and one who is free from lust—every one of them desires only what is beautiful, whether it be solid food or soft food; no one desires what is evil.”

“Great King, one who is not free from lust eats his food experiencing both the taste and the craving for the taste; but one who is free from lust eats his food experiencing the taste, yet without experiencing craving for the taste.
The seventh dilemma: The distinction between one with lust and one free from lust.
